summary:
Our project,
**Mars HAB**, is a concept for a safe and sustainable habitat where astronauts could live and work on Mars. We developed a modular living environment that combines radiation protection, recycled water, controlled air systems, hydroponic food production, solar energy, and robotic construction.

One of our main innovations is the **Bio-Air Wall**, a biological life-support concept that uses sealed algae bioreactor panels integrated into the habitat walls. The algae use light and water to absorb carbon dioxide and may contribute to oxygen production through photosynthesis. Sensors monitor temperature, pH, light, and gas levels, while an independent chemical and physical air-support system provides an additional safety layer.

Our project addresses the challenges of limited resources, harsh environmental conditions, and astronaut safety on Mars. It is important because it explores how biological technology, engineering, and resource recycling could work together to support more sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.
